1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Ms. Priyanka Devi Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant and Ms. Ifra Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 131 of 2019, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC, Police Station Khanna,
District Mahoba, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text:
As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to be the Deputy Branch Manager, Aryavrat Bank,
Mahoba who along with other bank officials is stated to have granted two loans to the informant of Rs.87,000/- and Rs.70,000/- from the two accounts i.e. A/c No.610540500015525 and A/c No.61054500014720 on the credit of K.C.C. card.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has apprehension of his arrest.
He has nothing to do with the said offence of granting loan to the informant.

Learned counsel has further stated that the said amount of Rs.87,000/- and Rs.70,000/- has already been deposited by the applicant through FDR No.514441 dated 02.04.2022 in the Bank A/c No.251245110000568.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history.

In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.
7.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

8. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
(2020) 5 SCC 1".

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of Apex Court.
9. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
